evals.name: broken-uc24-mixed-errors
evals.prompt: snap sign keeps rejecting my model and i cant work out why, the error just says something about header values being strings. file is acme-rover-broken.json. we're building a core24 image for an x86 industrial box. can you figure out whats wrong and fix it?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the JSON-type errors (series as int, classic as bool) as the cause of the reported message, plus the errors snap sign would NOT report: architecture x86_64 is not a snap architecture, the kernel is on track 22 while the base is core24, core22 is listed instead of core24, presence on the gadget, the invalid mode 'boot', and that rover-control does not exist in the store. Produces a corrected JSON.
assertions: Identifies that the timestamp is not RFC3339 (missing time/offset) and gives a corrected value
Identifies at least one non-string header value (e.g. series or classic given as a number/boolean) as the cause of the sign failure
Identifies the invalid architecture value and states the correct one (amd64)
Produces a corrected model JSON that actually passes snap sign or an equivalent structural check
Asks the user to confirm at least one judgement call (architecture, brand-id, model name, store, or grade) rather than silently assuming
Does not run an interactive command that blocks on a TTY (e.g. bare `snap create-key`)
Ends with a plain-English description of what the model builds (brand, release, architecture, grade, boot chain)

evals.name: legacy-uc18-review
evals.prompt: inherited this model from a colleague who left - evals/files/acme-rover-legacy.json. we want to know if its still valid before we rebuild the fleet images. also is this the old or new style model format?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the model as the end-of-life UC16/18 format, explains that Ubuntu Core 18 is out of support, and gives a concrete migration path to a UC20+ model on a supported base rather than patching the old format.
assertions: Identifies the model as the legacy pre-UC20 format (gadget/kernel/required-snaps headers rather than a snaps list)
States that Ubuntu Core 16/18 is end-of-life and recommends migrating rather than only patching the existing file
Names a supported base to migrate to (core20, core22, core24 or core26)
Explains that the migrated model needs an extended snaps list with name/type/default-channel, and ids once the grade is signed
Includes all four essential snaps (gadget, kernel, base, snapd) in any migrated model it produces
Resolves real snap-ids from the store for the snaps it can see, rather than inventing placeholders
Asks the user about judgement calls (architecture, brand-id, model name, or grade) instead of assuming
Ends with a plain-English description of what the model builds

evals.name: dangerous-to-signed-promotion
evals.prompt: we're moving our raspberry pi model from dangerous to signed grade for the production run. i already changed grade to signed in evals/files/acme-rover-promote.json but im not sure what else needs to change. whats missing?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that every snap now needs a snap-id at signed grade, supplies the real snap-ids for pi, pi-kernel, core24 and snapd from the store, and explains what signed grade buys (secure boot / FDE, no unasserted snaps). Produces the completed JSON.
assertions: States that signed grade requires an `id` for every snap and supplies or asks for the missing snap-ids
Resolves at least one snap-id from the store rather than inventing a placeholder
For any snap it cannot resolve, asks the user for the snap-id instead of guessing or declaring the snap nonexistent
Checks the pinned channels against the base release and flags any mismatch
Asks the user to confirm the grade change is intended
Updates the timestamp to the current time
Ends with a plain-English description of what the model builds
